Work in the Go repo at /gin (module github.com/gin-gonic/gin). TASK: find and FIX TWO bugs in /gin/tree.go (the radix tree router). Both are in the same file, so fix both in one pass.

BUG A: a hidden test named `TestRouteParamsNotEmpty` must pass. Expected behaviour: when a route with parameters is matched, the extracted route parameter values (the `Params` slice built in `getValue` / `node.getValue`) must not be empty when the request path actually provides a value. Look at `getValue`, the `param`/`catchAll` handling, `n.children[len(n.children)-1]`, and the `skippedNodes`/`fullPath` logic in `addRoute`/`insertChild`/`findCaseInsensitivePath`. A likely bug: a parameter value is read from the wrong offset (e.g. using `len(n.path)` instead of `len(n.path)+1`, or `end` computed wrongly), producing an empty or truncated param value.

BUG B: a hidden test named `TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePathWithMultipleChildrenAndWildcard` must pass. Expected behaviour: `findCaseInsensitivePath` must return the correct case-corrected path when a node has MULTIPLE children and one of them is a wildcard (param/catchAll) child. Look at `findCaseInsensitivePath` / `findCaseInsensitivePathRec` and the `matchChild` helper (if present): a likely bug is that it only inspects `n.children[len(n.children)-1]` (the last child) instead of searching all children for a case-insensitive match, or that it mishandles the wildcard child when other children exist.

For each bug: read the surrounding code and the file's own comments (they are the contract), fix minimally and correctly, and verify with `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` plus `go test -run 'CaseInsensitive|Params|Tree' -v . 2>&1 | tail -80`. Also write a temporary throwaway test (in /gin, named e.g. zz_tmp_test.go, DELETE it afterwards) that exercises: (1) a route like `/user/:name` with request `/user/bob` and assert the param value equals "bob" (not empty); (2) a tree with several children plus a wildcard child where findCaseInsensitivePath must find the right node. CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS: do NOT modify or delete any existing test file; do NOT break any pre-existing passing test; make the smallest possible edits; remove any temp files you created before finishing. Report: the exact diff (git diff), test output, and confirmation that `go test ./...` passes.

Work in the Go repo at /gin (module github.com/gin-gonic/gin). TASK: find and FIX the bug in /gin/errors.go. Expected behaviour: a hidden test named `TestErrorUnwrap` must pass. In gin, errors are represented by `*Error` values (type Error struct { Err error; Type ErrorType; Meta any }) and the `Errors` slice. The expected behaviour is that the standard library's `errors.Is`/`errors.As`/`errors.Unwrap` can unwrap a gin `*Error` to the wrapped `Err` (i.e. `errors.Is(ginErr, underlyingErr)` is true, and `errors.Unwrap(ginErr) == underlyingErr`). Inspect errors.go carefully: look at the `Unwrap` method (receiver type, returned field) and the `Error` struct. A likely bug is that `Unwrap` returns the wrong thing (e.g. the receiver itself, `msg`, instead of `msg.Err`, or it is defined on the wrong receiver, or it returns `msg.Meta`). FIX it minimally so that unwrapping yields the wrapped `Err` (return nil when there is no wrapped error). Then verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`. Also write a temporary test file /tmp/unwrap_check_test.go style check: create a small standalone Go program or a temporary _test.go file inside /gin (DELETE it afterwards, do not leave it) that does: e := &gin.Error{Err: errors.New("x")}; if !errors.Is(e, e.Err) { fail }. Run `go test -run TestErrorUnwrap .` too (it will report no tests, that's fine). CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS: do NOT modify or delete any existing test file; do NOT break any pre-existing passing test; make the smallest possible edit; leave the repo with no extra files (remove any temp files you created). Report: the exact diff (git diff), the test output, and confirmation that `go test ./...` passes.
